items.prompt: Which group of words is a main clause?

options.why: It starts with because and cannot stand alone.
It starts with when and cannot stand alone.
Although makes this depend on another clause.

hints: A main clause can stand alone as a sentence.
Subordinate clauses begin with words like because, when and although.
Which group makes sense on its own?
items.explanation: A main clause has a subject and a verb and makes sense by itself. The others need another clause.

items.prompt:
Which is the main clause in this sentence?

Although it was raining, Joko cycled to school.

options.why: This clause depends on the main clause.
This is only part of the subordinate clause.
This is missing the end of the main clause.

hints: Find the clause that could be a sentence alone.
Although signals the dependent clause.
Cover the Although part and read what is left.
items.explanation: Joko cycled to school makes sense on its own. Although it was raining depends on it.

items.prompt: Type the word that begins the subordinate clause. Citra stayed inside because it was raining.
hints: This subordinate clause begins with a conjunction.
Citra stayed inside is the main clause.
Which word starts the second part?
items.explanation: Because begins the subordinate clause, which gives the reason.

items.prompt:
Choose all the subordinate clauses in this sentence.

When the storm passed, Leo, who had been hiding, came out because he heard singing.

options.why: This is the main clause.

hints: A subordinate clause cannot stand alone.
Look for when, who and because.
The main clause is Leo came out.
items.explanation: Three clauses depend on the main clause Leo came out: one about time, one about who, and one giving a reason.

items.prompt: Sort each group of words into main or subordinate clauses.
hints: A main clause can stand alone.
Subordinate clauses begin with words such as although, unless, while.
Which groups could be full sentences?
items.explanation: The first three can stand alone. The last three begin with a conjunction and need a main clause.

items.prompt: A writer uses a very short sentence after several long ones: "The door closed." What effect does this have?

options.text: It creates a sudden pause and builds tension
It slows the story with extra detail
options.why: A short sentence has little detail, so it does not slow the story with description.

options.text: It gives the reader a list of facts
options.why: It gives only one event.

options.text: It shows the writer ran out of ideas
options.why: Writers choose short sentences for effect.

hints: Think about how it sounds after long sentences.
A short sentence stands out.
It makes the reader stop.
items.explanation: A short sentence after long ones stands out. It can create tension or surprise.

items.prompt: Read: "The mist drifted slowly over the quiet river, curling around the old boats and fading into the reeds." What effect does the long sentence create?

options.why: This long, flowing sentence feels slow, not fast.
A shock would usually come in a short sentence.
There are no steps or commands.

hints: Read it aloud and notice the pace.
The sentence keeps flowing, with several parts.
Calm words such as drifted and quiet help.
items.explanation: The long sentence and gentle verbs make the pace slow and the mood calm.

items.prompt: Which set of sentences best builds speed and panic?

options.text: The golden light spread across the quiet valley as the village woke slowly.
options.why: Long, calm sentences slow the pace.

options.text: It was a long and winding road that led to the old house.
options.why: This is a long sentence that slows the pace.

options.text: The children walked home, chatting about school and supper.
options.why: This is a calm scene.

hints: Short sentences make the pace quick.
Which choice has the shortest sentences?
Think about a chase.
items.explanation: A string of short, sharp sentences gives the feeling of speed and panic.

items.prompt: Sort each word by its word class.
hints: Nouns name things. Verbs show action. Adjectives describe nouns. Adverbs often end in ly.
Try the word in a sentence.
Start with swiftly: does it describe how someone moves?
items.explanation: Harbour and teacher are nouns, explore and decide are verbs, golden and ancient are adjectives, and quietly and swiftly are adverbs.

items.prompt:
In the sentence below, what word class is quickly?

The tiny frog leapt quickly.

options.why: An adjective describes a noun. Quickly describes the verb leapt.
It does not name a thing.
It does not show an action by itself.

hints: Ask: what does the word tell us?
It tells how the frog leapt.
Words that tell how, when or where an action happens are adverbs.
items.explanation: Quickly tells how the frog leapt, so it is an adverb.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses the word light as a verb?

options.why: Here light is a noun.
Here light is an adjective.
Here light describes breeze, so it is an adjective.

hints: A verb shows an action.
Ask what job the word does in each sentence.
Which one is an instruction to do something?
items.explanation: In Please light the candle, light is the action word, so it is a verb.

items.prompt: Match each word class to its purpose.
pairs: names a person, place or thing
shows where or when something is
hints: Each class does a different job.
Conjunctions join. Prepositions show position.
Start with noun: what does it name?
items.explanation: Each class has a job: nouns name, verbs act, adjectives describe nouns, adverbs often describe verbs, conjunctions join and prepositions show position.

items.prompt:
In the sentence below, what word class is under?

The cat hid under the bed.

options.why: A conjunction joins words or clauses. Under links the cat's position to the bed.
Under does not describe a noun.
It is not an action.

hints: Ask what the word shows.
It shows where the cat hid.
Words that show position before a noun are prepositions.
items.explanation: Under shows where the cat hid in relation to the bed, so it is a preposition.

items.prompt: Type the pronoun that replaces Amara and Tom. ___ are playing chess.
hints: A pronoun takes the place of a noun.
Amara and Tom are more than one person.
Which pronoun means more than one person?
items.explanation: They replaces Amara and Tom, so it is a pronoun.

items.answer: Although she was tired, Putri finished her essay.
hints: A complex sentence has a main clause and a subordinate clause.
The subordinate clause comes first and ends with a comma.
Start with Although.
items.explanation: Although she was tired is the subordinate clause. Putri finished her essay is the main clause.

items.prompt:
Which is the main clause?

Because the road was flooded, which meant a long detour, Dad decided to wait at the cafe.

options.why: This is a subordinate clause starting with because.
This is a subordinate clause starting with which.
This is incomplete without the rest of the clause.

options.text: Dad decided to wait at the cafe

hints: Find the clause that can stand alone.
Cross out the clauses beginning with because and which.
What is left is the main clause.
items.explanation: Dad decided to wait at the cafe can stand alone. The other two depend on it.

items.prompt: Read: "Hadi, who sat at the back, waved." What is the clause who sat at the back?

options.why: It cannot stand alone because who needs Hadi.

options.text: A subordinate clause that adds detail about Hadi

options.why: It is not a sentence by itself.
A clause has a subject and a verb. An adverb is a single word.

hints: Could who sat at the back be a sentence alone?
It starts with the relative pronoun who.
It adds extra information about Hadi.
items.explanation: The clause depends on the main clause and tells us more about Hadi. It is a subordinate (relative) clause.
